tagline: An old turnpike through a hill-town center.
intro: Litchfield Road comes in from the west as Route 118 and ends at Harwinton center, where Route 4 carries on along the same line east toward Rock Brook. This is the old Litchfield and Harwinton Turnpike, chartered in October 1798 to keep up the road between Litchfield, Harwinton and Burlington, and the main way between Hartford and Litchfield.

The town's name is made of the two towns that once held its land, Hartford and Windsor, with -ton on the end. It stayed a farm town all through the nineteenth century, having neither a railroad nor the water power to industrialize, and in the early twentieth century city people began building second homes here.

moments.title: Harwinton center
moments.text: The first meetinghouse stood right in the middle of the crossroads, and the Congregational Church nearby is a plain recreation of the 1808 sanctuary that burned in 1949.

moments.title: South Road
moments.text: Just south of the junction, William McConway of Pittsburgh, one of the early second-home people, had a run of fine quarry-stone walls built along the road.
